title: We Would Leave, O God, to Thee
description: We Would Leave, O God, to Thee in Tonic Solfa to VIENNA, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: William Gaskell wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 324, “Refuge in God”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to VIENNA; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: We would leave, O God, to Thee, Ev-ery anx-ious care and fear; Thou the trou-bled thought canst see, Thou canst dry the bit-ter tear.

lines: We would leave, O God, to Thee,
Thou the troubled thought canst see,
Thou canst dry the bitter tear.
Thou dost care for us, we know, —
Care with all a Father's love;
Thou canst make each earthly woe
On this faith we fain would rest;
Steadfast keep it in our breast,
Through each dark and trying hour.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Gaskell died in 1884.
credits: Words by William Gaskell (1805–1884), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to VIENNA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
